settlement_mapping.finding: Code matches the spec's settlement_mapping exactly: result='yes' -> payout 1.0, result='no' -> payout 0.0, result='scalar' -> payout read from settlement_value_dollars via fnum(), booked as WIN/LOSS via (fill.price - payout - fee) -- never VOID. If settlement_value_dollars is absent on a scalar result, the code logs a warning and defers (retries next cycle) rather than defaulting to zero or void, which is stricter than but consistent with the spec's intent ('never a void'). This correctly avoids the historical bug (scalar booked as VOID at $0) described in CLAUDE.md and golf_quirks_research/REPORT_P022_Settler_Scalar_Fix_2026-07-26.md. The generic KalshiGolfSettler in src/kalshi_golf_settler.py implements the equivalent fix for P-017 but is a separate code path and not what P-022 uses; the spec does not claim otherwise.

api_field_reliability.finding: The spec's entry_logic.close_reference_field_priority=['close_time','occurrence_datetime'] and its close_reference_rule ('close_time is the correct anchor ... REVERSE of the top-N quirk ... must never be inferred by analogy') is NOT what the shipped pod does and is NOT substantiated by current repo evidence -- it is actively contradicted. Two things established directly: (1) src/round_leader_fade_maker.py contains zero references to either close_time or occurrence_datetime anywhere in the file; its only close-reference mechanism is GolfScheduleResolver.resolve_event_close() from src/golf_schedule.py, an EXTERNAL ESPN-derived schedule. (2) src/golf_schedule.py's own docstring and research/REPORT_P022_Close_Time_2026-07.md state the opposite of the spec's claim: 'On an open round-leader market all six time fields (close_time, occurrence_datetime, expected_expiration_time, expiration_time, latest_expiration_time) collapse to one conservative ~20-day fallback; close_time is rewritten to the truth only at the instant the market closes' -- i.e. close_time is EQUALLY unreliable while the market is open, not a safe anchor, matching (not reversing) the general exchange-wide gotcha already documented in CLAUDE.md ('never a golf quirk'). What the spec describes matches only the FIRST, since-superseded fix from 2026-07-26 (P022_DECISION_RULE.md §11c: 'occurrence_datetime -> close_time' field-priority swap), which itself was found on 2026-07-27/28 to still be broken on open markets and was replaced by the external-schedule approach that is what actually ships. Presenting the superseded, still-broken field-priority rule as the current, correct, validated mechanism is exactly the class of error CLAUDE.md flags as having 'now cost P-022 two separate fixes' and the exact failure mode that produced 3 days of zero quotes (2026-07-23 to 2026-07-26/28). This is a factual defect in the spec, not merely an unmeasured item.

external_schedule_dependency.detail: src/golf_schedule.py's GolfScheduleResolver (ESPN public golf API, unauthenticated) is a hard dependency for P-022's entire placement-window logic -- there is no Kalshi-field fallback (see api_field_reliability finding above; the pod fails closed with no quote if the resolver returns None). Verified live 2026-08-02: GET site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/golf/pga/scoreboard?dates=2026 and GET .../leaderboard?league=pga&event=<id> both returned HTTP 200 with well-formed tournament/leaderboard/tee-time JSON. tests/test_golf_schedule.py asserts fail-closed behavior and the one-sided-early calibration on mocked data; live reachability was independently confirmed here rather than inferred from the tests.

blocking_issues: api_field_reliability check FAILED: the spec's stated close-time resolution mechanism (close_reference_field_priority preferring close_time over occurrence_datetime, described as 'the correct anchor' and 'the REVERSE of the top-N quirk') does not match the shipped implementation and is contradicted by src/golf_schedule.py, research/REPORT_P022_Close_Time_2026-07.md, and CLAUDE.md. The pod actually depends exclusively on an external ESPN schedule (src/golf_schedule.py) because close_time, like every other Kalshi time field, is a placeholder on an OPEN market -- it is not a reliable anchor on this family any more than on the top-N family. A reader relying on this spec's entry_logic to reproduce or extend P-022's timing logic would reintroduce the exact defect (structurally zero quotes) that was already fixed twice.
